summary: Sustained 5xx influx traced to apigw cgroup throttling and upstream SIGTERM churn
description: Issue summary: Beginning ~2026-03-13 09:20 UTC BrightBank observed a sustained elevation in 5xx responses on production chat endpoints. Initial spikes coincided with a keepalive sweep and an internal autoscaler activity window. Impact: Customers reported increased 502/503/504 rates and frequent streaming disconnects for long-poll sessions. Escalation: Customer-facing SLA impact for enterprise BrightBank. Environment: prod-us-east (multiple apigw frontends + regional serving runtime pool).
impact_details: Approximately 6% error-rate elevation for chat generation routes (route /v1/chat/*). Peak window 09:20-10:05 UTC, ~1200 requests/min for the tenant. Several long-lived streaming sessions experienced resets and subsequent retries leading to upstream overload. Internal metrics show apigw worker process CPU saturation and kernel cgroup throttling events on a subset of nodes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate BrightBank tenant traffic profile: 1k rps steady with ~5% long-lived streaming sessions using keepalive pings.
2) Trigger a keepalive sweep across apigw frontends (internal test harness: infra/loadgen/keepalive-sweep v2).
3) Observe apigw worker CPU / cgroup throttling counters and downstream 502/503 responses to client.
4) Reproduce on staging with same autoscaler topology to validate behavior.
investigation_notes: 09:28 - Support triage: customer reported rising 5xx rates; created ticket and routed to SRE on-call.
09:33 - SRE found elevated CFS throttling metrics on 3/12 apigw nodes (host-level cgroup.max_usage_us spikes). Kernel logs show repeated 'Task X blocked for more than 120 seconds' on worker threads.
09:42 - Correlated runtime logs: several serving-runtime processes received SIGTERM near the same timestamps and then restarted (graceful shutdown attempted but some sessions terminated mid-stream).
10:00 - Autoscaler events: a scheduled scale-in for a background batch job overlapped with prewarm activity, causing transient CPU pressure on shared hosts running apigw containers.

Hypothesis: a noisy background job + keepalive sweep caused host-level CPU contention, triggering cgroup throttling on apigw containers; throttling pushed request queues to the runtime, some runtime processes hit watchdog/timeouts and exited (SIGTERM chain), resulting in 502/503/504 amplification.
Evidence: host metrics, dmesg kernel OOM/blocked logs, apigw worker CPU and accept-queue growth charts in Grafana (links below).
timeline: 09:20 - BrightBank alerts show initial elevated errors
09:50 - Temporary mitigations applied (route-level rate limit, failover to warm pool)
10:12 - Customer reports partial recovery; error rate reduced but not fully stabilized
11:00 - Ongoing: deeper postmortem investigation scheduled; ticket remains In Progress
logs: serving-runtime-87 stderr: 'watchdog: runtime worker received SIGTERM, exiting (session count 34) at 2026-03-13T09:37:14Z'
apigw-frontend-12.log: 'ERROR downstream 502 upstream-reset after 120s queue-wait: txn=0x7f2b'
mitigation_actions: Applied a tenant-specific emergency route cap for BrightBank to 800 rps at 09:50 UTC to reduce downstream load
Force-failed a subset of apigw nodes into draining while shifting traffic to warm pool instances at 09:52 UTC
Disabled the background batch prewarm job on affected hosts to eliminate host CPU contention (temporary rollback)
Increased apigw container cpu_shares and raised cgroup CPU quota on impacted hosts as immediate relief
next_steps: SRE to run a controlled replay in staging to reproduce the cgroup-throttle + keepalive-sweep interaction (owner: Marco Silva)
Infra to add host-level guardrail that prevents batch-prewarm from co-locating with critical apigw containers (owner: Priya Desai)
Platform to add apigw healthcheck improvements: detect cgroup CPU-throttling early and divert traffic before runtime SIGTERM chain (owner: SRE)
Schedule postmortem and update runbook with mitigation patterns and capacity rules (owner: Engineering Leads)
Follow up with BrightBank CS contact with RCA draft and timeline by 2026-03-16
resolution: Temporary mitigations reduced error rate to baseline for BrightBank by routing through warm-pool and stopping the conflicting batch job. Full root cause analysis in progress; permanent fix pending changes to placement and cgroup guardrails.
